content.text:
What kind of story is The Nutcracker?

The Nutcracker is a story in which, on Christmas night, a nutcracker doll received as a gift comes to life and sets off with a girl named Clara to a land of wonder. Together with Tchaikovsky's ballet music, it's a classic beloved in wintertime.

content.alt: The Nutcracker - The original Nutcracker story
content.text:
The original Nutcracker story

Based on an 1816 novella by the German author E.T.A. Hoffmann, it became a world-famous classic when Tchaikovsky composed it as a ballet in 1892. It's full of fantastical scenes — the battle with the Mouse King, the journey to the Land of Sweets, the "Waltz of the Flowers," and more.

content.alt: The Nutcracker - A summary of the Nutcracker story
content.text:
A summary of the Nutcracker story

On Christmas night, the nutcracker doll Clara received comes to life and battles the Mouse King. With Clara's help he wins, and the doll transforms into a splendid prince who takes her to the Land of Sweets, where they receive a dazzling welcome. A night as beautiful as a dream unfolds.

content.alt: The Nutcracker - The moral of The Nutcracker
content.text:
The moral of The Nutcracker

The heart of it is the heart to summon courage and help a friend, and the joy that the world of imagination brings. Spark your child's imagination with, "If a gift came to life, what kind of adventure would you want to go on?"

content.alt: The Nutcracker - How to read it aloud to your child
content.text:
How to read it aloud to your child

Reading with Tchaikovsky's ballet music playing in the background brings the mood to life. Read the battle scene with excitement, and the Land of Sweets with wonder! Imagine together, "What kind of Land of Sweets would you want to visit?" Best suited for ages 4–7.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. What age is The Nutcracker good for?
A. It's best suited for ages 4–7. It's lovely to enjoy alongside the music and ballet during the Christmas season.

Q. Is it the same story as the ballet?
A. Yes. It weaves the storyline of Tchaikovsky's ballet, based on Hoffmann's novella, into a fairy tale.

Q. What activities go well with it?
A. Listening to the ballet music, drawing your imagined Land of Sweets, and decorating a nutcracker doll all work well.
